Center for Research Computing (CRC), University of Notre Dame

Proposes an approach; secondary: Evaluates — llm-wiki-memory-template, an agent-aware template of the llm-wiki pattern with a three-axis design framing; three deployed case studies + one design report, analysed by interpretive trace analysis

llm-wiki-memory-template (github.com/crcresearch/llm-wiki-memory-template; version Not stated), instantiating the llm-wiki pattern (Karpathy 2026; tonbi 2026). Overlays: Claude Code (validated end to end), Cursor (structurally only), 'none'; tutor variant (Case D)

LLM-maintained wiki of cross-linked Markdown pages with YAML frontmatter (type, up:, typed edges extends/supports/criticizes/source/related); home, index, log_<repo>.md (each entry with 'by: <human> via <agent>'), SCHEMA_<repo>.md; CLAUDE.md; agent-agnostic policy files discipline-gates.md and verification-gate.md (pre-commit checklist); agent overlay commands/skills/rules (.claude/, .cursor/); ALWAYS_FILES sync allowlist. Append-only convention

Bootstrap (scripts/instantiate.sh) -> ongoing operations: ingest (wiki-experiment, wiki-source), query, lint; discipline gates and verification gate before commit; one commit per log entry; template sync via update-from-template.sh; three-tier governance (base / variant / derived) with graduation trigger
Verification gate as pre-commit checklist (applied by agent); humans read/audit the wiki and log; Case B retroactive audit by a human researcher. No mandatory human approval step stated
Full template in real projects (Cases A, B, D with Claude Code); Case C multi-agent only as design (not run)
Not classifiable (project memory/knowledge wiki, not a software specification)
Mixed knowledge work: research software projects (retrieval research; adaptive web scraper), course wiki for teaching; not code-generation tasks as such
fields.why: The cases are knowledge-work wikis attached to research and teaching projects; whether the code bases were new or existing is not stated (Project R 'instantiated from the template', Project F built in parallel with the template)
fields.doubt: Os casos são wikis de projetos de investigação e ensino; o artigo não diz se o código parte do zero ou de projeto existente. Confirma nas secções 5.1–5.4 ou aceita 'misto/não indicado'.
